newsitem.title: USA: NYC police reject contract offer by city - paper.
newsitem.headline: NYC police reject contract offer by city - paper.

text.p: The leaders of New York City's largest police union rejected the Giuliani Administration's contract offer, which could lead to months of arbitration and police protests, the New York Times reported Wednesday.
City officials said their offer would raise police salaries about 16 percent over five years, a larger five-year increase than the 13.3 percent one that civilian employees got two years ago.
During 1995 and and 1996, no raises would have been granted to the police officers.

The city's offer would in five years make New York City police salaries comparable with those now paid in Nassau County and set up a two-tier system, under which new officers would have to work more days a year than current ones, the paper said.

The P.B.A. has been without a contract since March 30, 1995, and until recently, refused to negotiate with the city as it won Albany's approval for a state board to resolve contract disputes. But the state's highest court ruled the action unconstitutional, the Times said.
